title: Overtime Pay Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Weekly pay with overtime — regular hours, overtime hours and your multiplier. Enter your hourly rate, regular hours worked, overtime hours worked and overtime multiplier and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Work out a week's pay when some of it is overtime. Enter your hourly rate, your regular hours and your overtime hours, and the calculator pays the regular hours at your normal rate and the overtime hours at your multiplier — time-and-a-half (1.5×) is the default, the rate the US Fair Labor Standards Act requires for hours over 40 in a week. It also shows the effective hourly rate across the whole week, so you can see what the overtime is really worth.

## How to use the Overtime Pay Calculator

Start by entering your hourly rate, then entering your regular hours worked, entering your overtime hours worked and finally entering your overtime multiplier (×). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your normal hourly rate.
2. Enter the regular hours and the overtime hours you worked.
3. Set the multiplier — 1.5 for time-and-a-half, 2 for double time.
4. Read the regular pay, overtime pay and total for the week.

## Formula

Regular pay = rate × regular hours. Overtime pay = rate × multiplier × overtime hours. Total = regular pay + overtime pay. Effective rate = total ÷ total hours.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. At $25 an hour with 40 regular hours and 10 overtime hours at time-and-a-half: regular pay is $1,000, overtime pay is $375, total weekly pay is $1,375, and the effective rate across the 50 hours is $27.5 an hour. Try the same figures in the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Hourly rate: 25, Regular hours worked: 40, Overtime hours worked: 10, Overtime multiplier: 1.5 ×), the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) returns Regular pay: $1,000, Overtime pay: $375, Total weekly pay: $1,375, Total hours: 50, Effective hourly rate: $27.5. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## When overtime is owed

Under the US Fair Labor Standards Act, most hourly workers must be paid at least 1.5× their regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek. Some states and contracts are more generous — California, for example, also requires overtime after 8 hours in a day and double time after 12. Salaried exempt workers are generally not covered, and the rules differ by state, so check your local law if the numbers here do not match your payslip.

## Double time and other multipliers

Some jobs pay double time (2×) for Sundays, holidays or very long shifts. The multiplier field accepts any value, so set 2 for double time or 1.25 for a smaller premium. The effective hourly rate shows what the whole week worked out to per hour — useful for comparing a week with overtime against a normal week.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Time-and-a-half (1.5×) is the legal minimum for most US hourly workers over 40 hours.
- Check your payslip: overtime is usually shown as a separate line at the higher rate.
- A week of heavy overtime raises the effective rate — compare it with your base rate before agreeing to extra shifts.

## Frequently asked questions

### How is overtime pay calculated?

Overtime hours are paid at the multiplier times your normal rate. At $25 an hour with 10 overtime hours at time-and-a-half, the overtime pay is $25 × 1.5 × 10 = $375, on top of $1,000 of regular pay. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) and start straight away.

### What is time-and-a-half?

Pay at 1.5 times your normal hourly rate — the standard overtime premium. At $20 an hour, time-and-a-half is $30 an hour. Double time is 2 times the rate. Try it with your own numbers in the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### After how many hours is overtime paid?

Under US federal law, hours over 40 in a workweek. Some states add daily overtime — for example California requires overtime after 8 hours in a day — and some contracts set their own thresholds. Try it with your own numbers in the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Overtime Pay Calculator use?

Regular pay = rate × regular hours. Overtime pay = rate × multiplier × overtime hours. Total = regular pay + overtime pay. Effective rate = total ÷ total hours. You can see it in action in the [Overtime Pay Calculator](/overtime-pay-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
